fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Into a Dating Quiz
fields.features_subheading: The quiz, its result screens, and the table every play lands in come from one prompt, with email tagging wired in where you ask for it.
fields.feature_1:
Each answer mapped to a dating style

Name the styles you want the quiz to sort into, such as Spark Chaser or Slow Burn. Emergent writes the questions and result screens, and a prompt remaps any option's style.
fields.feature_2:
Emails tagged by result

The result screen can ask for an email, and the app tags each address with the style it came with. Connected through its API, your newsletter tool files that tag as a segment.
fields.feature_3:
Every play saved as a row

Each finished quiz lands as a row in a database you own: the picks, the style, the email if one was left, and the time. Filter a month by style before you write the next issue.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Takers tap through one question at a time with a progress bar, a flow that suits a link in a bio or a group chat. Emergent puts no cap on how many people can take the quiz.
fields.feature_5:
Tallies and reminders on a schedule

Ask for a Monday email with the week's results by style, or a Slack alert when a taker leaves an address. Before an event, a reminder can chase every RSVP that has no result.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and code you can keep

Publish the quiz on a custom domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it for the next season.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Dating Quizzes With Four Different Jobs
fields.tab_content_1:
212 plays feed a list that sorts itself

Anjali Rhee put a dating quiz on First Light Coaching's site in March, and 212 people finished it. The result screen names the taker's style, asks for an email, and tags it with the result. 78 landed on Spark Chaser, so that segment's welcome sequence opens with pacing advice instead of generic tips.
fields.tab_content_2:
After four reminders, the name tags print

Dockside Social ends its RSVP form with a six-question dating quiz, and each guest's style goes on their name tag as an icebreaker. Before October's mixer, 44 of 48 RSVPs had a result. Any RSVP with no quiz result gets an email at 9:00 the morning of, and the last 4 answered before Farrah Keane printed the tags.
fields.tab_content_3:
One filter turns a 31-client book into 6

Quillwood Introductions runs its intake as a dating quiz plus a short form, so every client sits in one table with a style, what they are looking for, and dealbreakers. When Iduna Maddox asks for someone who dates on purpose, Zora Demir filters 31 active clients down to 6 Intentional Daters before their first call.
fields.tab_content_4:
90 answers come in without any names

The New Chapter Letter, a newsletter for readers dating again after a divorce, runs the quiz every October, and the app saves each answer with no names attached. 90 readers took it this year: 52 leaned toward taking more time, 38 toward getting back out there. The November issue led with one piece for each result.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Dating Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan, write, and test a dating quiz whose results people trust, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the styles before the questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep the options the same size
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the quiz is for before writing a question: capturing emails for a coaching list, breaking the ice at an event, opening a matchmaking intake, or giving readers a result worth forwarding. The job decides the questions, the results, and what each play saves.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write 3 to 5 dating styles first and give each one a short, kind description. Every question you write later has to sort people between them. Merge or cut any style you cannot tell apart from its neighbor at this stage.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Build each question around something a person does: the first date they would pick, the text they send after a good one, what their profile leads with. People answer scenarios more honestly than questions that ask which style they think they are.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give every question one option per style, written at the same length and in the same tone. When one option is longer or more flattering than the rest, takers pick it for the wording, and the result stops meaning anything.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Open each result with what the answers lean toward, add two or three lines that feel specific to that style, and close with one thing to try on the next date. A result that reads like a compliment with homework gets shared; a verdict gets closed.
fields.howto_step_6_des: List the fields before you build: the picks, the style, the time, and an email only when something follows it, such as a guide for that style. Put the list in your prompt, and the table under the quiz matches it from the first play.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test the quiz as every style
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run through it four times, aiming for a different style each run, and check each one comes out on top when it should. Then read every result page aloud. A line you would not say to a friend's face comes out before launch.

faq_plan.a: A dating quiz is a short set of questions that sorts the taker into a result, such as a dating style, or scores what they know about dating. The ones coaches and event hosts run are matching quizzes, where each option counts toward a style, like the eight-question quiz on this page.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dating quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt: the questions, the style each option points to, and what each play saves. Emergent's AI survey builder writes the quiz, the result screens, and the database behind it. Publish it on your site, send one link, and change any question by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free dating quiz builder with no response caps?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. There are no response caps at any tier, and hosting on your own domain uses credits.

faq_plan.q: What are good dating quiz questions to ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask about choices: the first date someone would pick, the text after a good one, what a profile leads with. Map each option to one style, the way a spirit animal quiz maps every pick to an animal. Keep it to 8 or 10 questions; the quiz on this page uses 8.

faq_plan.q: How do dating coaches use a dating quiz to get clients?
faq_plan.a: As a lead magnet. The quiz names the visitor's style, the result screen asks for an email, and each address lands in a segment for that style. The follow-up sequence then speaks to how that person dates instead of reading like a blast sent to everyone.

faq_plan.q: Should a dating quiz end in a style or a score?
faq_plan.a: End it in a style when the takers are singles playing for insight: a named result reads as something to share, not a grade. Keep scores for knowledge formats, where answers are right or wrong. In a matching quiz every option maps to a result, and nobody fails it.

faq_plan.q: Can a dating quiz work as an icebreaker at a singles event?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put a short quiz at the end of the RSVP and print each guest's result on their name tag, and first conversations start themselves. For a mixed room of couples and friends, a friendship quiz gets the whole crowd playing. Chase missing results with a reminder the morning of the event.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a dating quiz that stays kind?
faq_plan.a: Write every result as a leaning, never a verdict: your answers lean toward taking it slow, not you are too guarded. Skip questions about age, body, and income. Close each result with one thing to try, never something to fix, and read it as if the taker were across the table.

faq_plan.q: What should the result screen of a dating quiz show?
faq_plan.a: The style name, two or three sentences on what the answers lean toward, and a next step the taker can use this week. Ask for an email only if a follow-up will arrive. On Emergent the result screen is part of the build, and a prompt rewords it in place.

faq_plan.q: Can a dating quiz send a different follow-up for each result?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Map each style to its own sequence, the way a career quiz pairs each result with fields of work to explore. The app tags every finished play with its result, your newsletter tool reads the tag through its API, and a Slow Burn never gets the Spark Chaser email.

quiz.title: Dating Quiz: How Do You Date?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you meet people, plan dates, and decide what comes next. Your result names the dating style your answers lean toward, with one thing to try on your next date.

questions.text: A match suggests meeting up. What is your ideal first date?

options.text: A long walk and real questions
Whatever sounds fun that afternoon
Coffee with someone I already sort of know
Trivia night where my friends will be

questions.text: How do you usually meet the people you date?

options.text: On apps, with a clear idea of what I want
A conversation that starts out of nowhere
Friendships that slowly turn into more
Parties, group trips, and friends of friends

questions.text: After a good first date, what do you do?

options.text: Take a day, then suggest a specific plan
Text on the way home while the night is fresh
Wait and see how the week of texting feels
Tell the group chat everything first
Someone who asks where this is going
Banter that lands on the first try
Feeling at ease, like you have met before
Someone my friends immediately like

questions.text: How often do you want to be going on dates?

options.text: A couple a month, each one chosen carefully
Whenever the spark shows up
Rarely, until someone feels worth it
Weekends, somewhere lively, rarely alone

questions.text: A date goes just okay. What happens next?

options.text: A kind, clear message that it is not a match
Nothing. If it were right, I would feel it
A second chance. Okay can grow on me
A debrief with friends before I decide

questions.text: What does your dating profile lead with?

options.text: What I am looking for, stated plainly
One great photo and a one-line opener
Hobbies I would happily share with someone
Group photos from the last trip

questions.text: What is your idea of a great love story?

options.text: Two people who chose each other on purpose
A chance meeting that rearranged the week
Best friends who figured it out in year three
Introduced by friends at a wedding

results.title: The Intentional Dater
results.description: Your answers lean toward dating on purpose: you know what you are looking for and ask the questions that find it. That clarity saves everyone time. Try leaving one evening unplanned and let a date be only fun; direction works best with a little room in it.

results.title: The Spark Chaser
results.description: Your answers lean toward chemistry first: you trust a great conversation and decide quickly. Try one second date the first did not quite earn, and see what shows up once the fireworks settle.

results.title: The Slow Burn
results.description: Your answers lean toward comfort that builds: you date best once someone stops feeling like a stranger. Try naming what you want a little earlier than feels natural, and the right person will know to stay.

results.title: The Social Dater
results.description: Your answers lean toward meeting people where the energy is: group tables, trivia nights, friends of friends. Try one quiet one-on-one date a month; some people only open up away from the crowd.
